page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.26xlarge is a high-capacity, storage-optimized instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance supplies 104 dedicated vCPUs along with 768.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 7.38 GB of RAM per virtual core.

The primary architectural focus of this server is local storage throughput and capacity. It integrates 23,038 GB of direct-attached local solid-state drive (SSD) storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps. The instance does not include GPU accelerators and does not offer complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In terms of resource density, pairing expansive local SSD storage with substantial memory and core counts delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for systems that would otherwise incur high external block storage I/O expenses. The instance configuration is structured for heavy data workloads, such as distributed NoSQL databases, search indexing engines, transactional relational databases, and high-throughput real-time data processing clusters.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.26xlarge is a high-density, storage-optimized compute instance designed for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running via a KVM hypervisor, it features 104 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.38 GB of RAM per vCPU, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps. The instance bundles 23,038 GB of local SSD capacity directly on the host, maximizing local read and write operations without reliance on separate networked block devices. It contains no GPU accelerators. The combination of dense multicore processing, large memory capacity, and expansive local solid-state storage makes this server well matched for high-throughput distributed databases, real-time analytics platforms, large-scale search clusters, and transactional database infrastructure.
